Proposed detection system is a complex solution incorporating a dominant color based segmentation technique of a football playfield, a 3D playfield modeling algorithm based on Hough transform and a dedicated algorithm for player tracking. Evaluation of the system is carried out using SD (720 × 576) and HD (1280 × 720) resolution test material. Additionally, performance of the proposed system is tested with different lighting conditions (including non-uniform pith lightning and multiple player shadows) and various camera positions.

articleTitle: ADC for mixed-signal SoC
publicationTitle: ICSES 2010 International Conference on Signals and Electronic Circuits
abstract: Circuit design of pulse-potential ADC with a small quantity of passive and active components is worked out for mixed-signal SoC. The main error convention fractions of that kind are examined and it is shown that potential accuracy surpasses traditional ADC. The appropriateness of using a multidifferential operational amplifier in such interfaces is shown. The modeling results of schematic circuit ADC on analog basic matrix chip components immune to radiation are adduced.

articleTitle: Orthogonal implementation of two-dimensional separable denominator systems
publicationTitle: ICSES 2010 International Conference on Signals and Electronic Circuits
abstract: In the paper, a realization technique for two-dimensional orthogonal separable-denominator systems is presented. It starts with orthogonal state-space equations and finish with a structure consisting of Givens rotations and unit delays. Obtained result is suitable for FPGA-based implementation for which a Givens rotation design was proposed, suitable for realtime processing. The technique is illustrated with a design of separable-denominator Gaussian filter.

articleTitle: Phase offset in CMA and MMA soft switching blind equalization schemes — a comparative study
publicationTitle: ICSES 2010 International Conference on Signals and Electronic Circuits
abstract: The paper presents simulation analyses of the CMA and the MMA blind equalization methods in the presence of a constant phase offset. A soft switching mechanism between a blind mode and the decision-directed (DD) one is applied for reduction of linear distortion in communication system. The performed experiments have the form of a comparative study of two closely related blind equalization methods working in an exemplary single carrier transmission system with square QAM modulation. Influence of a phase offset on equalization performance and the functionality of the switch procedure are examined.

articleTitle: Broadband quarter-square 4Q analog multiplier based on CMOS inverters
publicationTitle: ICSES 2010 International Conference on Signals and Electronic Circuits
abstract: This paper concerns a quarter-square analog 4Q (four-quadrant) multiplier based on own, yet already published, core architecture using four CMOS inverters. An emphasis on control circuits operating at low voltage and highspeed has been put, and therefore the presented circuit solution is suitable for RF applications in communication systems. Operation at high-speed is possible thanks to the architecture containing simple building blocks based on CMOS inverters and using CMOS transistors with sufficiently large biasing currents. Circuit-level design and simulation, circuit layout, post-layout verification for UMC's 180 um CMOS process has been done on the base Foundry Design Kit in the Cadence DF II environment.

articleTitle: A wideband variable gain amplifier with feedback DC-offset correction in 0.13µm CMOS technology
publicationTitle: ICSES 2010 International Conference on Signals and Electronic Circuits
abstract: A low power and area optimized wideband variable gain amplifier (VGA) has been designed in 0.13 μm CMOS technology for an integrated Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) receiver. The VGA consists of three gain stages. The first stage is a resistively loaded, fixed gain source coupled pair, while the other two are variable gain degenerated differential pairs. Each stage also utilizes negative Miller capacitance to extend the bandwidth, resulting in a VGA configuration with -3 dB bandwidth of 1 GHz. The gain of the VGA can be continuously varied from 10 dB to 30 dB. The input-referred noise density is 2.8 nV/√Hz and the out-of-band IIP3 is -1 dBm. The circuit consumes only 5.25 mW from a 1.2 V supply (excluding the output buffer) and occupies 0.037 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> die area.

articleTitle: System on chip verification strategy based on FDL mechanism
publicationTitle: ICSES 2010 International Conference on Signals and Electronic Circuits
abstract: The paper deals with problem of the formal verification of complex electronic embedded systems. A new com-monsense strategy is proposed. The formal methodology of the inference engine modeling based on Fuzzy Default Logic is given. The multistage verification strategy as the platform dependent verification (PDV) toolset is defined. The methodology has been validated on examples on a prototype AMBA-based virtual SoC platform working with SystemVerilog verification procedures. The advantages of the presented methodology have been emphasized.

articleTitle: Digital analysis methods of wheezes in asthma
publicationTitle: ICSES 2010 International Conference on Signals and Electronic Circuits
abstract: The systems of e-health are powerful tools in medical domain. The main advantage of those systems is reducing the requirement of hospital care and the number of mortalities. Modern e-health systems can control successfully such diseases as cardiac, diabetic or pulmonary diseases. This article is a review of wheeze breath detection algorithms in asthma monitoring techniques. The proposition of new solution of wheezes detection system is presented as well.

articleTitle: The concept of CMOS OOK transmitter using low voltage self-oscillating active inductor
publicationTitle: ICSES 2010 International Conference on Signals and Electronic Circuits
abstract: This paper presents a low voltage, On-Off Keying (OOK) CMOS integrated transmitter for ISM 434 MHz biomedical applications using a concept of a novel self-oscillating (degenerated) active inductor. A thorough theoretical analysis of the oscillator is presented, together with simulated results using UMC 90 nm 1P9M RF process libraries. The proposed oscillator achieves an average phase noise of -93 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset from 434 MHz carrier frequency, with a relative tuning range of 26% to compensate for process variations. The transmitter allows modulation speeds up to 100 Mbps with RF output power of -4 dBm to 50 Ω load from 1 V power supply.

articleTitle: An influence of signal amplitude variation on interpolated DFT method
publicationTitle: ICSES 2010 International Conference on Signals and Electronic Circuits
abstract: In order to obtain high accuracy of frequency measurement via DFT the interpolated DFT method is used. This method makes assumption that measured signal is periodical, particularly with constant amplitude. In this paper an influence of amplitude variation on Interpolated DFT method is analyzed. It occurs that for some decreasing signals amplitude changes are insignificant for Interpolated DFT.

articleTitle: Electric circuits exercise and learning assessment system using databases
publicationTitle: ICSES 2010 International Conference on Signals and Electronic Circuits
abstract: In this paper, we describe an electric circuits exercise and test system with the learning assessment that facilitate the assessment task of lecturers. We advance the development of the educational support teaching material enhanced more by adding ”Exercise” and ”Test” insufficient in the previous iCASS (Interactive Circuits And System Seminar). In ”Exercise”, students learn electric circuit through web-browser embedding Java-applet. Learning results in exercise is appreciable from various aspects. In ”Test”, students take test of electric circuits and the result of test is summarized in the table and graph automatically by database. Lecturer can grade each students based on it.
